chapters.title: Isaac and the First Festival of Booths
chapters.html:
Jubilees 16

1On the new moon of the fourth month we appeared to Abraham at the oak of Mamre, and we talked with him, and we told him that a son would be given to him by Sarah his wife.

2Sarah laughed, for she heard that we had spoken these words with Abraham[; and we rebuked her, and she became afraid and denied that she had laughed at the words].

3We told her the name of her son, as it is ordained and written on the tablets of heaven — Isaac —

4and that when we returned to her at the set time, she would have conceived a son.

5In this month the Lord executed His judgment on Sodom and Gomorrah and Zeboiim and all the region of the Jordan, and He burned them with fire and sulfur and destroyed them to this day[, even as I have told you all their works: how they were wicked and very great sinners, and unclean, committing impurity in their flesh and doing abominations on the earth].

6In the same way the Lord will execute judgment on the places where they do as the uncleanness of Sodom, like the judgment of Sodom.

7But Lot we saved, for the Lord remembered Abraham, and brought him out from the middle of the overthrow.

8He and his daughters also committed a sin on the earth such as had not been on the earth from the days of Adam until then, for the man lay with his daughter.

9Here — it has been commanded and engraved concerning all his seed on the tablets of heaven, to remove them and root them out, and to execute judgment on them like the judgment of Sodom, and to leave him no seed of man on the earth on the day of judgment.

10In this month Abraham moved from Hebron, and went and lived between Kadesh and Shur, in the mountains of Gerar.

11In the middle of the fifth month he moved from there and lived at the Well of the Oath.

12In the middle of the sixth month the Lord visited Sarah and did for her as He had said.

13She conceived and bore a son in the third month, in the middle of the month, at the time the Lord had told Abraham; on the festival of the first fruits of the harvest Isaac was born.

14Abraham circumcised his son at eight days old; he was the first to be circumcised according to the covenant that is ordained forever.

15In the sixth year of the fourth week we came to Abraham at the Well of the Oath, and we appeared to him, as we had told Sarah that we would return to her, and she would have conceived a son.

16We returned in the seventh month and found Sarah with child before us, and we blessed her and told her all that had been decreed for him: that he would not die until he had fathered six more sons, and would see them before he died[; but in Isaac his name would be multiplied and called].

17All the seed of his sons would become nations and be counted with the nations[; but from the sons of Isaac one would become a holy seed, and would not be counted among the nations].

18For he would become the portion of the Most High, and all his seed had fallen into the possession of God, to be for the Lord a people treasured above all peoples, and to be a kingdom and a priesthood and a holy people.

19We went on our way, and we told Sarah all that we had told him, and they both rejoiced with very great joy.

20He built an altar there to the Lord, who had delivered him and was making him rejoice in the land where he lived as a guest[; and he kept a festival of joy in this month for seven days beside the altar].

21He built booths for himself and for his servants at this festival, and he was the first to keep the Festival of Booths on the earth.

22During these seven days he offered every day, day by day, on the altar a burnt offering to the Lord: two bulls and two rams, seven sheep, one male goat for sin, to make atonement with it for himself and for his seed.

23As a peace offering: seven rams and seven kids, seven sheep and seven male goats, and their grain offerings and their drink offerings; and he burned all their fat on the altar[, an offering for a soothing aroma].

24Morning and evening he burned fragrant incense: frankincense and galbanum and stacte, nard and myrrh, spice and costus. All seven of these he offered, crushed and mixed in equal parts, and pure.

25He kept this festival seven days, rejoicing with all his heart and with all his soul, he and all who were in his house; and there was no foreigner with him, nor anyone who was uncircumcised.

26He blessed his Creator, who had created him in his generation, for He had created him for His good pleasure; for he knew and perceived that from him would come the plant of righteousness for the eternal generations, and from him a holy seed, to be like the One who made all things.

27He blessed and rejoiced, and he called the name of this festival the festival of the Lord, a joy acceptable to God Most High.

28We blessed him forever, and all his seed after him through all the generations of the earth, because he kept this festival in its season, according to the testimony of the tablets of heaven.

29For this reason it is ordained on the tablets of heaven concerning Israel that they shall keep the Festival of Booths seven days with joy, in the seventh month, acceptable before the Lord, a law forever through their generations, every year.

30To this there is no limit of days, for it is ordained forever concerning Israel that they should keep it and live in booths, and set wreaths on their heads, and take leafy boughs and willows of the brook.

31Abraham took branches of palm trees and the fruit of splendid trees, and every day he went around the altar with the branches seven times; in the morning he rose early and praised and gave thanks to his God for everything with joy.

Notes

  • Words in [brackets] — not in either Ge'ez text here, which is cut short in these verses. In vv5, 16, 17, 20 and 23 they follow the Latin, which begins partway through v5; the opening words of v5's bracket, even as I have told you, come from Charles, where the Latin is broken. In v2 the bracket follows Charles's English, made from other Ge'ez manuscripts.

  • vv1–4 the visit at Mamre — Genesis 18:10–15: At the appointed time I will return to you, at the time of life, and Sarah shall have a son… Sarah denied it, saying, "I did not laugh" — for she was afraid. In Genesis the three visitors eat with Abraham; in Jubilees they are the angels of the presence, and they name the child from the tablets of heaven.

  • vv5–9 Sodom and Lot — Genesis 19:24–29: The LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah sulfur and fire… God remembered Abraham, and He sent Lot out from the midst of the overturning. v8 "with his daughter" — so the EOTC; Charles and the Latin have daughters. v9 "all his seed" — Lot's seed, Moab and Ammon (Genesis 19:37–38). The Greek sums it up: from Lot came the Moabites and Ammonites, an accursed seed from an unlawful union.

  • vv10–11 "between Kadesh and Shur… the Well of the Oath" — Genesis 20:1, he settled between Kadesh and Shur, and he lived as a guest in Gerar. The Well of the Oath is Beersheba: Therefore that place was called Beersheba, for there the two of them swore (Genesis 21:31).

  • vv12–14 Isaac's birth — Genesis 21:1–4: The LORD attended to Sarah as He had said… Abraham circumcised Isaac his son at eight days old. Jubilees dates it to the festival of first fruits, the Festival of Weeks, the day of the covenants with Noah and Abram (6:17; 14:10; 15:1). v13 "in the third month" — so the Ge'ez and Charles; the Latin has the seventh month.

  • vv15–16 the dates — the sixth year of the fourth week is 40 × 49 + 3 × 7 + 6 = 1987, the year after the covenant of 15:1 (1986), and so the year of Isaac's birth. Yet v16 finds Sarah with child in its seventh month, after a birth in the third. The text is left as it stands.

  • v16 "we blessed her and told her" — so the EOTC; Charles and the Latin have him, Abraham, and v19 says the angels then told Sarah all that we had told him. "six more sons" — the sons of Keturah, Genesis 25:1–2. "in Isaac his name would be multiplied and called" — the Latin; Genesis 21:12 has through Isaac shall seed be called for you.

  • vv17–18 "a people treasured above all peoples… a kingdom and a priesthood and a holy people" — Exodus 19:5–6: you will be My own treasure out of all the peoples… You will be for Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. Of Abraham's sons only Isaac's line, and of Isaac's sons only one, is kept out of the nations.

  • vv20–31 the first Festival of Booths — Abraham keeps it at the Well of the Oath in the seventh month, before the law is given. Leviticus 23:40–42: you shall take for yourselves the fruit of splendid trees, branches of palm trees, boughs of leafy trees, and willows of the brook… You shall live in booths for seven days. Jubilees adds the wreaths on the head (v30) and the sevenfold circling of the altar (v31); the Greek has the circling with branches of palm trees and olive trees.

  • v24 the seven spices — Exodus 30:34 names four of them for the incense of the tabernacle: stacte and onycha and galbanum… and pure frankincense. Each shall be in equal measure. "stacte" — the Ge'ez māya ləbn; "spice" — sanbalt, which the Latin gives as spica, spikenard.

  • v26 "for he knew" — the Latin takes it as Abraham; Charles has He, God. "the plant of righteousness" — the name 1 Enoch gives the chosen line: the plant of righteousness and uprightness forever (1 Enoch 93:5).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Latin and Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Hagar Sent Away, and Mastema's Challenge
chapters.html:
Jubilees 17

1In the first year of the fifth week of this jubilee Isaac was weaned, and Abraham made a great feast in the third month, on the day his son Isaac was weaned.

2Ishmael, the son of Hagar the Egyptian, was before the face of Abraham his father, in his place; and Abraham rejoiced and blessed the Lord, because he had seen his sons and had not died without sons.

3He remembered the word He had spoken to him on the day Lot parted from him[; and he rejoiced because God had given him seed on the earth to inherit it, and with all his mouth he blessed the One who created all things].

4Sarah saw Ishmael playing and dancing, and Abraham rejoicing with great joy, and she was jealous of Ishmael[; and she said to Abraham, "Drive out this slave woman and her son, for the son of this slave woman shall not inherit with my son Isaac."]

5The word was grievous in Abraham's eyes, because of his maidservant and because of his son, that he should drive them away from him.

6The Lord said to Abraham, "Let it not be grievous in your eyes over the boy and over the slave woman. All that Sarah says to you — listen to her words and do it, for through Isaac shall name and seed be called for you.

7As for the son of this slave woman, I will make him into a great nation, for he is of your seed."

8Abraham rose early in the morning and took bread and a skin of water, and set them on the shoulders of Hagar and the child, and sent her away.

9She went and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba, and the water was finished from the skin, and the child was thirsty and could not go on, and fell down.

10His mother took him and cast him under an olive tree, and went and sat opposite him, about a bowshot away, for she said, "Let me not see the death of my child"; and as she sat she wept.

11An angel of God, one of the holy ones, said to her, "Why are you weeping, Hagar? Rise, lift up the child and hold him in your hand, for the Lord has heard your voice and has seen the child."

12She opened her eyes and saw a well of water, and she went and filled her skin with water and gave her child a drink[; and she rose and went toward the wilderness of Paran].

13The child grew and became an archer, and the Lord was with him; and his mother took a wife for him from the daughters of Egypt.

14She bore him a son, and he called his name Nebaioth, for she said, "The Lord was near to me when I called on Him."

15And it came to pass in the seventh week, in its first year, in the first month of this jubilee, on the twelfth of this month, that there were words in heaven about Abraham[, that he was faithful in all that He told him, and that he loved the Lord, and that in every affliction he was faithful].

16The prince Mastema came and said before God, "Here — Abraham loves Isaac his son and delights in him above all[. Tell him to offer him as a burnt offering on the altar, and You will see whether he does this command, and You will know whether he is faithful in everything in which You test him]."

17The Lord knew that Abraham was faithful in every affliction He told him of; for He had tested him with his land and with famine, and had tested him with the wealth of kings[, and had tested him again with his wife, when she was taken from him, and with circumcision; and had tested him with Ishmael and Hagar his maidservant, when he sent them away].

18In everything in which He had tested him he was found faithful, and his soul was not impatient, and he was not slow to act, for he was faithful and a lover of the Lord.

Notes

  • Words in [brackets] — not in either Ge'ez text here, which is cut short in these verses. In vv3 and 4 they follow the Latin, which covers vv1–5 of this chapter; in vv12, 15, 16 and 17 they follow Charles's English, made from other Ge'ez manuscripts. Without v4's bracket Sarah never asks for Hagar to be sent away, and without v16's Mastema never says what the test should be.

  • vv1–14 Hagar and Ishmael sent away — Genesis 21:8–21, retold in order, in this project's wording where the Ge'ez allows: Drive out this slave woman and her son, for the son of this slave woman shall not inherit with my son, with Isaac… through Isaac shall seed be called for you (21:10, 12). v4 "playing and dancing" — so the Ge'ez; the Latin has playing with Isaac; Genesis 21:9 has only laughing, the verb of Isaac's name.   • v13 "his mother took a wife for him" — the EOTC writes for them, lomu; the second Ge'ez text has the same. v14 "Nebaioth" — Ishmael's firstborn in Genesis 25:13. The name is explained from The Lord was near; Genesis gives no reason for it.

speech.text: Jubilees 17
In the first year of the fifth week of this jubilee Isaac was weaned, and Abraham made a great feast in the third month, on the day his son Isaac was weaned.
Ishmael, the son of Hagar the Egyptian, was before the face of Abraham his father, in his place; and Abraham rejoiced and blessed the Lord, because he had seen his sons and had not died without sons.

He remembered the word He had spoken to him on the day Lot parted from him[; and he rejoiced because God had given him seed on the earth to inherit it, and with all his mouth he blessed the One who created all things].

Sarah saw Ishmael playing and dancing, and Abraham rejoicing with great joy, and she was jealous of Ishmael[; and she said to Abraham, "Drive out this slave woman and her son, for the son of this slave woman shall not inherit with my son Isaac."]
The word was grievous in Abraham's eyes, because of his maidservant and because of his son, that he should drive them away from him.

The Lord said to Abraham, "Let it not be grievous in your eyes over the boy and over the slave woman. All that Sarah says to you — listen to her words and do it, for through Isaac shall name and seed be called for you.
As for the son of this slave woman, I will make him into a great nation, for he is of your seed."
Abraham rose early in the morning and took bread and a skin of water, and set them on the shoulders of Hagar and the child, and sent her away.
She went and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba, and the water was finished from the skin, and the child was thirsty and could not go on, and fell down.
His mother took him and cast him under an olive tree, and went and sat opposite him, about a bowshot away, for she said, "Let me not see the death of my child"; and as she sat she wept.
An angel of God, one of the holy ones, said to her, "Why are you weeping, Hagar? Rise, lift up the child and hold him in your hand, for the Lord has heard your voice and has seen the child."
She opened her eyes and saw a well of water, and she went and filled her skin with water and gave her child a drink[; and she rose and went toward the wilderness of Paran].
The child grew and became an archer, and the Lord was with him; and his mother took a wife for him from the daughters of Egypt.
She bore him a son, and he called his name Nebaioth, for she said, "The Lord was near to me when I called on Him."

And it came to pass in the seventh week, in its first year, in the first month of this jubilee, on the twelfth of this month, that there were words in heaven about Abraham[, that he was faithful in all that He told him, and that he loved the Lord, and that in every affliction he was faithful].

The prince Mastema came and said before God, "Here — Abraham loves Isaac his son and delights in him above all[. Tell him to offer him as a burnt offering on the altar, and You will see whether he does this command, and You will know whether he is faithful in everything in which You test him]."

The Lord knew that Abraham was faithful in every affliction He told him of; for He had tested him with his land and with famine, and had tested him with the wealth of kings[, and had tested him again with his wife, when she was taken from him, and with circumcision; and had tested him with Ishmael and Hagar his maidservant, when he sent them away].
In everything in which He had tested him he was found faithful, and his soul was not impatient, and he was not slow to act, for he was faithful and a lover of the Lord.

chapters.title: The Binding of Isaac
chapters.html:
Jubilees 18

1The Lord said to him, "Abraham, Abraham!" He said, "Here I am."

2He said to him, "Take your son, your beloved one, whom you love — Isaac — and go to the high land, and bring him up on one of the mountains that I will show you."

3He rose early in the morning and saddled his donkey, and took his two young men with him, and Isaac his son, and split the wood for the offering, and went to the place on the third day[; and he saw the place from far off].

4He came to a well of water, and said to his young men, "Stay here with the donkey, and I and the boy will go; and when we have bowed down, we will return to you."

5He took the wood of the offering and set it on Isaac his son, and he took in his hand the fire and the knife[; and the two of them went together to that place].

6Isaac said to his father, "Father!" [He said, "Here I am, my son." He said to him, "Here is the fire and the knife and the wood — but where is the lamb for the burnt offering, father?"]

7He said, "The Lord will see to the lamb for the burnt offering for Himself, my son." [He came near to the place of the mountain of God.]

8He built an altar and set the wood on the altar, and bound Isaac his son and set him on the wood that was on top of the altar, and stretched out his hand to take the knife to slaughter Isaac his son.

9I stood before him and before the prince Mastema, and the Lord said, "Tell him not to lay his hand on the boy or do anything to him, for I know that he fears the Lord."

10I called to him from heaven and said to him, "Abraham!" He was terrified and said, "Here I am."

11I said to him, "Do not lay your hand on the boy or do anything to him, for now I know that you fear the Lord, and you have not withheld your son, your firstborn, from Me."

12The prince Mastema was put to shame. Abraham lifted up his eyes and looked, and here — a ram caught by its horns; and Abraham went and took the ram and brought it up as a burnt offering in place of his son.

13Abraham called that place "The Lord Has Seen," so that it is said, "The Lord has seen." That is Mount Zion.

14The Lord called Abraham by his name a second time from heaven, as He made us appear to speak to him in the name of the Lord.

15He said, "By Myself I have sworn, says the Lord: because you have done this thing, and have not withheld your son, your firstborn, whom you loved, from Me[, blessing, I will bless you, and multiplying, I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven and as the sand that is on the seashore; and your seed will inherit the cities of its enemies].

16In your seed all the nations of the earth will be blessed, because you listened to My voice[; and I have shown to all that you are faithful to Me in all that I have said to you. Go in peace]."

17Abraham went to his young men, and they rose and went together to Beersheba[; and Abraham lived at the Well of the Oath].

18He kept this festival every year, seven days with joy, and he named it the festival of the Lord, after the seven days in which he went and returned in peace.

19So it is ordained and written on the tablets of heaven concerning Israel and its seed, to keep this festival seven days with the joy of a festival.

Notes

  • Words in [brackets] — not in either Ge'ez text here, which is cut short in these verses. In vv15, 16 and 17 they follow the Latin, which begins at v10 of this chapter; in vv3, 5, 6 and 7 they follow Charles's English, made from other Ge'ez manuscripts. The Ge'ez of v6 stops at Isaac's Father!; his question about the lamb, and the answer the Ge'ez keeps in v7, are the heart of Genesis 22:7–8.

  • vv1–19 the binding of Isaac — Genesis 22:1–19, retold in order, in this project's wording where the Ge'ez allows: Take, please, your son — your beloved one — whom you have loved — Isaac (22:2); God will see to the lamb for a burnt offering for Himself, my son (22:8). Jubilees adds what Genesis does not tell: Mastema stands watching (v9), and he is put to shame (v12).

  • v1 "Abraham, Abraham!" — Genesis 22:1 calls him once; the double call is Genesis 22:11, the angel's. Here the order is turned about: v10, the angel's call, has the name once in the EOTC (Charles and the Latin have Abraham, Abraham).

  • v2 "the high land" — Genesis 22:2 has the land of Moriah.

  • vv9, 11 "I know" — so the Ge'ez, as in Genesis 22:12, now I know that you fear God. Charles and the Latin have I have shown: in their text the test is not for God to learn but for the watching Mastema to see, as in v16, I have shown to all that you are faithful to Me.

  • vv11, 15 "your firstborn" — so the EOTC, of Isaac, though Ishmael is older; the Latin has firstborn in v11 and only son in v15. Genesis 22:12, 16 has your beloved one (see the note there).

  • v13 "That is Mount Zion" — Genesis 22:14 ends On the mountain of the LORD it will be seen. Jubilees names the mountain. So does Chronicles: Solomon began to build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, on Mount Moriah (2 Chronicles 3:1). The Greek has where David later established the sanctuary.

  • vv15–16 "By Myself I have sworn" — Genesis 22:16–18. "will inherit the cities of its enemies" — the Latin; Genesis has Your seed shall seize the gate of their enemies.

  • vv18–19 "this festival… seven days" — the Ge'ez does not name it. The heavenly council met on the twelfth of the first month (17:15); counted from there, three days' journey out and seven days in all would fall in the week of the Festival of Unleavened Bread, which Leviticus sets on the fifteenth day of this month… Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread (Leviticus 23:6). v18 "every year" — the Latin has three times each year.

chapters.title: Sarah's Death, and Abraham Blesses Jacob
chapters.html:
Jubilees 19

1In the first year of the first week of the forty-second jubilee Abraham returned and lived opposite Hebron, that is Kiriath-arba, two weeks of years.

2In the first year of the third week of this jubilee the days of Sarah's life were completed, and she died in Hebron.

3Abraham went to weep for her and to bury her. [We tested him, to see whether his spirit was patient and not faint in the words of his mouth; and he was found very patient in this too, and was not troubled.]

4For with patience of spirit he spoke with the sons of Heth, that they might give him a place to bury his dead in.

5The Lord gave him favor before all who saw him[; and he entreated the sons of Heth in meekness, and they gave him the field of the double cave, which is opposite Mamre — that is Hebron — for four hundred pieces of silver].

6They pleaded with him, saying, "We will give it to you for nothing"; but he would not take it from their hands for nothing, for he gave the price of the place, the silver in full[; and he bowed down before them twice, and after this he buried his dead in the double cave].

7All the days of Sarah's life were one hundred and twenty-seven years, that is, two jubilees and four weeks and one year; these are the days of the years of Sarah's life.

8This is the tenth trial with which Abraham was tried, and he was found faithful, patient in spirit.

9He did not say a word about the promise of the land, that the Lord had said He would give it to him and to his seed after him[; and he begged a place from them to bury his dead, for he was found faithful, and he was written on the tablets of heaven as the friend of God].

10In its fourth year he took a wife for Isaac his son, and her name was Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nahor, Abraham's brother, the sister of Laban and daughter of Bethuel; and Bethuel was the son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother.

11Abraham took for himself a third wife, named Keturah, from the daughters of his household servants, for Hagar had died before Sarah.

12She bore him six sons, Zimran and Jokshan and Medan and Midian and Ishbak and Shuah, in two weeks of years.

13In the sixth week, in its second year, Rebekah bore Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. Jacob was whole and upright, and Esau was a fierce man, a man of the field, and hairy; and Jacob lived in tents.

14The young men grew, and Jacob learned writing; but Esau did not learn, for he was a man of the field and a hunter, and he learned war, and all his deeds were fierce.

15Abraham loved Jacob, and Isaac loved Esau.

16Abraham saw Esau's deeds, and he knew that through Jacob name and seed would be called for him[; and he called Rebekah and gave her commands about Jacob, for she loved Jacob more than Esau].

17He said to her, "My daughter, watch over my son Jacob, for he will be in my place on the earth, and for a blessing among the sons of men, and for the glory of all the seed of Shem.

18For I know that the Lord will choose him to be a people for His own possession, above all who are on the face of the earth.

19Here — Isaac my son loves Esau more than Jacob, but I see that you love Jacob in truth.

20Add still more kindness to him, and let your eyes be on him in love[; for he will be a blessing for us on the earth, from now on and to every generation of the earth].

21Let your hands be strong, and let your heart rejoice in your son Jacob[; for I have loved him above all my sons. He will be blessed forever, and his seed will fill all the earth].

22If a man can number the sand of the earth, so also will his seed be numbered.

23All the blessings with which the Lord has blessed me and my seed will belong to Jacob and to his seed all the days.

24In his seed my name will be blessed, and the name of my fathers, Shem and Noah and Enoch and Mahalalel and Enosh and Seth and Adam.

25These will serve to lay the foundations of heaven, and to strengthen the earth, and to renew all the lights that are in the expanse."

26He called Jacob before the eyes of Rebekah his mother, and kissed him and blessed him and said,

27"Jacob, my beloved son, whom my soul loves, may God bless you from above the expanse, and give you all the blessings with which He blessed Adam and Enoch and Noah and Shem, and all that He has told me[, and all that He promised to give me; may He make them cleave to you and to your seed forever, according to the days of heaven above the earth].

28May the spirits of Mastema not rule over you or over your seed, to turn you away from following the Lord, who is your God, from now on and forever.

29May the Lord God be a father to you, and you His firstborn son and His people, all the days.

30[Go in peace, my son."] The two of them went out together from Abraham.

31Rebekah loved Jacob with all her heart and with all her spirit, very much more than Esau; and Isaac loved Esau much more than Jacob.

Notes

  • Words in [brackets] — not in either Ge'ez text here, which is cut short in these verses. In vv3, 5, 6, 9, 16, 20 and 21 they follow the Latin, which covers this chapter as far as v26; in vv27 and 30 they follow Charles's English, made from other Ge'ez manuscripts. Without the brackets of vv5–6 the Ge'ez never says where Sarah was buried.

  • vv1–7 the dates — the first year of the forty-second jubilee is 41 × 49 + 1 = 2010; the first year of its third week, when Sarah dies, is 2024. v7 "two jubilees and four weeks and one year" — 98 + 28 + 1 = 127, the years of Genesis 23:1: The life of Sarah was a hundred years and twenty years and seven years. The Latin has four weeks minus one year, which comes to 125.

  • vv3–9 the tenth trial — Genesis 23 tells the purchase of the cave at length; Jubilees makes it a test of patience. Abraham, who has been promised the whole land, buys a grave in it and says nothing. "the double cave" — the Latin's name for the cave Genesis calls Machpelah, which it takes as double: the cave of the field of Machpelah, facing Mamre — that is Hebron (Genesis 23:19).

  • v9 "the friend of God" — Isaiah 41:8: the seed of Abraham My friend; James 2:23: he was called friend of God. Here the name is written on the tablets of heaven.

  • v10 "Bethuel was the son of Milcah" — the Ge'ez runs together here (wa-Batuʾel waladomu la-Batuʾelāwiyān, "and Bethuel fathered the Bethuelites"); the sense follows the Latin and Charles. Genesis 22:20: Milcah has borne sons, she also, to Nahor your brother. "In its fourth year" — 2027; Isaac, born in 1987, is forty, as in Genesis 25:20, Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah.

  • vv11–12 Keturah — Genesis 25:1–2. Jubilees makes her a daughter of the household servants, and has Hagar die before Sarah; Genesis says neither.

  • vv13–14 Jacob and Esau — Genesis 25:27: Esau was a man who knew hunting, a man of the field; and Jacob was a whole man, dwelling in tents. Jubilees adds that Jacob learned to write and Esau learned war. The date — the second year of the sixth week is 2046, when Isaac is fifty-nine; Genesis 25:26 has Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them, and the Greek of this verse says the same.

  • vv15–31 Abraham chooses Jacob — in Genesis Abraham's death is told before the twins are born (Genesis 25:7–8), and the blessing reaches Jacob through Rebekah's plan, when Isaac's eyes are dim (Genesis 27:1). In Jubilees Abraham sees the boys grow up and sets his blessing on Jacob himself, with Rebekah as its keeper. v16 "through Jacob name and seed would be called for him" — the words of 16:16 and Genesis 21:12, through Isaac shall seed be called for you, carried on to the next generation.

  • v24 "Shem and Noah and Enoch and Mahalalel and Enosh and Seth and Adam" — Abraham's line, skipping many names; the Latin leaves out Seth.

  • v25 "to lay the foundations of heaven, and to strengthen the earth" — as the LORD says to His people in Isaiah 51:16: to plant the heavens and to lay the foundations of the earth, and to say to Zion, "You are My people."

  • v29 "a father to you, and you His firstborn son" — Exodus 4:22: Israel is My son, My firstborn.

chapters.title: Abraham Commands His Sons
chapters.html:
Jubilees 20

1In the forty-second jubilee, in the first year of the seventh week, Abraham called Ishmael and his twelve sons, and Isaac and his two sons, and the six sons of Keturah and their sons.

2He commanded them to keep the way of the Lord, to do righteousness, and to love each one his neighbor, and to be so in every strife, each walking toward the others so as to do justice and righteousness on the earth;

3that they should circumcise their sons according to the covenant He had made with them, and not turn aside to the right or the left from all the ways the Lord commanded us; and that we should keep ourselves from all fornication and uncleanness, and put away from among us all uncleanness and fornication.

4If any woman or girl among you commits fornication, burn her with fire; and let them not go whoring after their eyes and their hearts, and let them not take wives for themselves from the daughters of Canaan, for the seed of Canaan will be uprooted from the land.

5He told them of the judgment of the giants and the judgment of Sodom, how they were judged for their wickedness, and died for fornication and uncleanness and corruption among themselves through fornication.

6"You too, keep yourselves from all fornication and uncleanness, and from all the defilement of sin, so that you do not make our name a curse, and all your life a hissing, and all your sons a ruin by the sword, and become cursed like Sodom, and all your remnant like the sons of Gomorrah.

7I testify to you, my sons: love the God of heaven and cling to all His commandments, and do not go after their idols and after their uncleanness.

8Do not make for yourselves molten gods or carved images, for they are empty[, and there is no spirit in them, for they are the work of hands, and all who trust in them trust in nothing. Do not serve them, and do not bow down to them].

9But serve the Most High God and bow down to Him always, and hope for His face at all times, and do righteousness and uprightness before Him, so that He may be pleased with you and give you His mercy and send down rain for you morning and evening[, and bless all your works that you do on the earth, and bless your bread and your water, and bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your land, the herds of your cattle and the flocks of your sheep].

10You will be a blessing on the earth, and all the nations of the earth will desire you[, and they will bless your sons in my name, so that they may be a blessing as I am]."

11He gave gifts to Ishmael and his sons and to the sons of Keturah, and sent them away from Isaac his son, and he gave everything to Isaac his son.

12Ishmael and his sons, and the sons of Keturah and their sons, went together and lived from Paran to the entrance of Babylon, in all the land toward the east, facing the desert.

13These mixed with one another, and their name was called Arabs and Ishmaelites[, to this day].

Notes

  • Words in [brackets] — not in either Ge'ez text here, which is cut short in these verses. They follow the Latin, which begins partway through v5: vv8, 9, 10 and 13.

  • v1 the date — the first year of the seventh week of the forty-second jubilee is 41 × 49 + 6 × 7 + 1 = 2052. By the book's date for Abraham's birth (1876, 11:15) he is 176; Genesis 25:7 gives him a hundred years and seventy years and five years in all. His death comes in chapter 23.

  • v2 "to keep the way of the Lord, to do righteousness" — Genesis 18:19: he may charge his sons and his house after him, and they shall keep the way of the LORD, to do righteousness and judgment. Jubilees shows him doing it. "in every strife" — the Ge'ez has ṣabʾ, war or strife; Charles reads among all men.

  • v4 "burn her with fire" — the law of Leviticus 21:9 for a priest's daughter who prostitutes herself: She shall be burned in the fire. "go whoring after their eyes and their hearts" — Numbers 15:39: you will not go about after your own heart and your own eyes, which you follow like a prostitute. "the daughters of Canaan" — Abraham's charge in Genesis 24:3, here given to all his sons.

  • v5 "the giants" — the sons of the Watchers (5:1; 7:22), destroyed with Sodom as the two great examples of judgment.

  • v6 "a hissing" — so the Latin and Charles; the EOTC has la-təmkəḥt, the word rendered glory at 19:17, which does not fit a curse.

  • v9 "rain… morning and evening" — the Latin has the early and the late rains, as Deuteronomy 11:14: I will give the rain of your land in its season, the early rain and the late rain. "the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your land" — Deuteronomy 28:4: Blessed is the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground.

  • vv11–13 the sons sent east — Genesis 25:5–6: Abraham gave all that was his to Isaac. To the sons of the secondary wives… Abraham gave gifts, and he sent them away from Isaac his son… eastward, to the land of the east. Jubilees adds that the sons of Ishmael and of Keturah mixed together and became the Arabs. "Paran" — the EOTC writes Farmon; the Latin has Faramon.

speech.text: Jubilees 20
In the forty-second jubilee, in the first year of the seventh week, Abraham called Ishmael and his twelve sons, and Isaac and his two sons, and the six sons of Keturah and their sons.

He commanded them to keep the way of the Lord, to do righteousness, and to love each one his neighbor, and to be so in every strife, each walking toward the others so as to do justice and righteousness on the earth;

that they should circumcise their sons according to the covenant He had made with them, and not turn aside to the right or the left from all the ways the Lord commanded us; and that we should keep ourselves from all fornication and uncleanness, and put away from among us all uncleanness and fornication.

If any woman or girl among you commits fornication, burn her with fire; and let them not go whoring after their eyes and their hearts, and let them not take wives for themselves from the daughters of Canaan, for the seed of Canaan will be uprooted from the land.

He told them of the judgment of the giants and the judgment of Sodom, how they were judged for their wickedness, and died for fornication and uncleanness and corruption among themselves through fornication.

"You too, keep yourselves from all fornication and uncleanness, and from all the defilement of sin, so that you do not make our name a curse, and all your life a hissing, and all your sons a ruin by the sword, and become cursed like Sodom, and all your remnant like the sons of Gomorrah.
I testify to you, my sons: love the God of heaven and cling to all His commandments, and do not go after their idols and after their uncleanness.

Do not make for yourselves molten gods or carved images, for they are empty[, and there is no spirit in them, for they are the work of hands, and all who trust in them trust in nothing. Do not serve them, and do not bow down to them].

But serve the Most High God and bow down to Him always, and hope for His face at all times, and do righteousness and uprightness before Him, so that He may be pleased with you and give you His mercy and send down rain for you morning and evening[, and bless all your works that you do on the earth, and bless your bread and your water, and bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your land, the herds of your cattle and the flocks of your sheep].
You will be a blessing on the earth, and all the nations of the earth will desire you[, and they will bless your sons in my name, so that they may be a blessing as I am]."
He gave gifts to Ishmael and his sons and to the sons of Keturah, and sent them away from Isaac his son, and he gave everything to Isaac his son.
Ishmael and his sons, and the sons of Keturah and their sons, went together and lived from Paran to the entrance of Babylon, in all the land toward the east, facing the desert.
These mixed with one another, and their name was called Arabs and Ishmaelites[, to this day].
